Sara — thanks for the clear list and the attachment. High level note: we can support three distinct delivery patterns that map to typical regulated deployments: 

1) Private (customer-managed hardware or air-gapped private deployment) — full data custody, on-prem or colocated; Redwood provides control plane only or optionally ships a private bundle.
2) Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPUs) — physical GPU pools reserved for your tenancy within our colo; network isolation and contract-backed data handling.
3) Hybrid (recommended for POC) — customer VPC + Redwood-managed dedicated GPUs in an isolated tenancy with strict egress policies; faster to stand up than full on-prem.

I'll put a short comparison workbook together and include a recommended hybrid fleet layout (tiling and breakpoints) plus preliminary week-by-week procurement timeline. See attached: proposed_hybrid_fleet_layout.xlsx and cost_model_q2.csv (draft).

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik to provide technical tiling and latency implications (by tomorrow morning).
- Marissa to draft commercial buckets (commit vs burst) and SLA notes (by tomorrow afternoon).
- I'll assemble a 1-page decision checklist for your security team before your Wednesday meeting.

Can you share a preferred time for a 30-minute alignment call on Tuesday?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hannah — quick technical note to support the hybrid recommendation. Key tradeoffs and recommended defaults for MediLine's workload profile (high QPS inference, median prompt length ~120 tokens, occasional long-context batches):

- GPU tiling and instance class:
  * Preferred: 8xA100-80GB-style slices (or equivalent LLM-optimized accelerators) for predictable KV-cache and throughput. Good balance of latency and batch efficiency.
  * Alternative for cost-constrained POC: mixed tiling with some 4x-slices + aggressive quantization (int8) for non-critical routes.

- Cache & Batching: enable prefix KV cache for clinical templates and continuous batching for bulk inference windows (2–5s latency SLO for low-latency endpoints).

- Data residency/egress: for hybrid we can place the runtime in Redwood-managed tenancy but enforce VPC peering with strict egress rules (no S3 access outside your tenant). This reduces provisioning time vs on-prem while meeting most audit requirements.

- Provisioning timeline estimates (engineering lead time):
  * Hybrid dedicated pool (initial capacity 10 tiles): 7–10 business days after contracts & infra access.
  * Fully private (air-gapped): 4–6 weeks (hardware procurement or on-site install plus validation).

- Operational fallbacks: automatic model variant fallback to quantized variants on capacity pressure + routing policies to failover to lower-cost reserved tiles with identical model versions.

I'll attach a short tiling spreadsheet after I finalize the exact instance family choices.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Hi Sara & team — looping in commercial details and attachments as promised. Summary of options (pricing buckets are illustrative, final numbers will follow in the SOW):

Option A — Hybrid (recommended for POC)
- Setup: Redwood-managed dedicated tiles in an isolated tenancy + VPC peering and egress controls.
- Lead time: 7–10 business days after contracts and IAM access.
- Pricing: weekly buckets available for 4–12 week pilots; monthly committed discount for 12+ weeks.

Option B — Redwood Dedicated (fully reserved)
- Setup: reserved GPU pools (Redwood-managed) with stronger contractual isolation.
- Lead time: 10–14 business days.
- Pricing: monthly reserved commitments; lower unit price at scale.

Option C — Private / On-prem
- Setup: customer-managed hardware (we offer an on-site bundle or deployment assistance).
- Lead time: 4–6 weeks.
- Pricing: license + support + optional managed services.

Attached are: MediLine_SOC2_evidence_request.xlsx (filled where applicable) and cost_model_q2.csv (high-level). For procurement: please confirm which contract term you prefer (pilot 6 weeks vs 12 weeks vs annual commit) so we can firm up the purchase order path and SLA addenda.
